title: Finite Quantization, Lloyd Iteration, and Compact Companders

items.title: The weighted centroid minimizes finite-cluster squared error
items.statement: For positive finite weights and a nonempty cluster, squared error equals the centroid cost plus total cluster weight times squared distance from the centroid; an empty cluster has zero cost for every center.
items.strategy: Expand the squared norm and use the vanishing weighted centered sum; check uniqueness and the empty-cluster convention.

items.title: Cumulative coordinate of a point density on a compact interval
items.statement: For a positive normalized C1 point density g on [a,b], define G_g(x)=integral_a^x g(t)dt using the Riemann integral of a continuous function.
items.strategy: State the nondegenerate interval, positivity, C1 regularity, normalization and integral convention.

items.title: Finite measurable squared-error quantizer and nearest-center rule
items.statement: Define finite Borel index maps with a finite reproduction tuple, expected squared-error distortion under a finite-second-moment Borel law, and the least-index nearest-center specialization with its cell inequalities.
items.strategy: Specify the Borel domain, finite discrete index set, Euclidean squared norm, source moment and tie rule.

items.title: A positive C1 point density has a C2 cumulative inverse
items.statement: A positive normalized C1 g on a nondegenerate compact interval has a strictly increasing C2 cumulative map G_g:[a,b]->[0,1] and a C2 inverse with phi'=1/(g composed with phi) and phi''=-g' composed with phi divided by (g composed with phi)^3.
items.strategy: Use the primitive theorem, mean value theorem, IVT, uniqueness of inverse values and explicit difference quotients; derive the second derivative and endpoint extensions.

items.title: The finite nearest-center quantizer is Borel with finite distortion
items.statement: For a Borel probability law on R^d with finite second moment and a finite center tuple, the least-index nearest-center cells are Borel and the expected squared error is finite, including coincident centers and empty cells.
items.strategy: Express cells by strict/nonstrict inequalities of continuous squared-distance polynomials and dominate squared error by twice the source and center squared norms.

items.title: Positive C1 compact one-dimensional compander
items.statement: For positive normalized C1 densities f,g on [a,b], use inverse cumulative boundaries phi(j/N) and reproduction points phi((j-1/2)/N), with half-open cells and the final right endpoint included; define the exact squared-error distortion.
items.strategy: State fixed compact support, normalized positive densities, the cumulative inverse, every boundary and reproduction point, and the absence of overload.

items.title: Exact finite-data Lloyd quantizer
items.statement: On positive weighted finite data, repeatedly assign by least-index nearest center, replace nonempty centers by weighted centroids, leave empty centers unchanged, and stop when the exact center tuple is unchanged.
items.strategy: Specify input, exact comparison/arithmetic model, deterministic ties, empty-cluster branch, stop test and output.

items.title: Exhaustive global empirical squared-error quantizer
items.statement: Enumerate the k^N assignments, use weighted centroids on nonempty clusters and x_1 on empty clusters, retain the first least-cost assignment, and return nearest-center reassignment.
items.strategy: Specify the exact finite search order, empty-cluster convention, cost and output.

items.title: The compact compander is a measurable finite quantizer
items.statement: The compander's consecutive interval cells are Borel and partition [a,b], its finite index map is measurable, and its squared-error distortion is finite for each N.
items.strategy: Use strict monotonicity of the cumulative inverse, half-open interval cells, compact support and the bound |x-r_j|<=b-a.

items.title: Exact finite-data Lloyd descent and finite termination
items.statement: A center-changing pass strictly decreases empirical distortion; at most 2^(Nk) passes occur, ending at a nearest-assignment/centroid fixed point, with an exponential exact-operation bound and no global-optimum assertion.
items.strategy: Use assignment minimization, the weighted centroid excess identity, the finite set of possible center values, and deterministic fixed-point stopping.

items.title: Exhaustive empirical search attains a global quantizer
items.statement: The k^N assignment enumeration terminates and returns a nearest-center tuple whose empirical squared-error distortion is no greater than every k-center tuple; its operation count is exponential.
items.strategy: Compare every tuple's nearest assignment, its centroid-adjusted cost, the exhaustive minimum, and the returned tuple's nearest reassignment.

items.title: Exact high-rate limit for a positive compact one-dimensional compander
items.statement: For positive normalized C1 source and point densities on a fixed compact interval, N^2 D_N(f,g) converges to (1/12) integral_a^b f/g^2.
items.strategy: Transform each cell to cumulative coordinates; derive a uniform second-order midpoint expansion and sum its cubic leading terms; pass to midpoint Riemann sums and transform back.

items.title: Optimal point density within the compact compander class
items.statement: Among positive normalized C1 point densities, g*=f^(1/3)/integral f^(1/3) uniquely minimizes the compact compander coefficient at (1/12)(integral f^(1/3))^3.
items.strategy: Normalize f/g^3 against the density g and integrate the exact factorization z+2-3z^(1/3)=(z^(1/3)-1)^2(z^(1/3)+2); check equality and admissibility.

title: Finite Quantization, Lloyd Iteration, and Compact Companders — Examples

items.title: Lloyd can stop at a strictly suboptimal finite-data fixed point
items.statement: Equal weights on {0,1,4,5,9} and initial centers (5/2,9) stop at distortion 17/5, while centers (1/2,6) have distortion 29/10.
items.strategy: Calculate every strict nearest comparison, verify the first centers are the assigned centroids, and compute the smaller alternative cost exactly.

items.title: Uniform density gives exact midpoint compander distortion
items.statement: For f=g=1 on [0,1], midpoint quantization has exact distortion 1/(12N^2), so N^2 D_N=1/12 and agrees with the compander limit.
items.strategy: Integrate squared distance on each of the N equal symmetric cells and sum exactly.
